name: 1Password
whatYouLose: Audited cryptography and a security team on call
Autofill across every browser and mobile OS
Secure sharing, recovery and breach monitoring
The peace of mind that comes from not rolling your own crypto
prompt:
Do not build a password manager from scratch. Instead, set up a self-hosted Vaultwarden server with the official Bitwarden clients.

Tasks:
- Write a docker-compose.yml for Vaultwarden behind Caddy with automatic HTTPS on my domain.
- Disable open signups, enable the admin panel with an Argon2 hashed token, configure SMTP for invites.
- Nightly encrypted backups of the data directory to S3-compatible storage with restic, and a tested restore script.
- Fail2ban rules for the login endpoint.
- A README covering upgrades, restore drills and how to connect the Bitwarden browser extension and mobile apps.
Done when: a fresh machine can restore the vault from backup using only the README.
notes: This is the one category where "build it yourself" is bad advice. The prompt sets up an audited open-source alternative instead.
